its noun is a latent (mustatir) pronoun, its implied form being "هو", referring to the wall. ﴿لِغُلامَيْنِ﴾: the two are attached (mutaʿalliq) to the omitted khabar (predicate). ﴿يَتِيمَيْنِ﴾: a naʿt (adjective). ﴿فِي الْمَدِينَةِ﴾: the two are attached to an omitted naʿt of غلامين. ﴿وَكانَ﴾: the wāw is conjunctive, and an incomplete past verb. ﴿تَحْتَهُ﴾: an adverb of place attached to the omitted, fronted khabar, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿كَنْزٌ﴾: the noun of كان. ﴿لَهُما﴾: the two are attached to an omitted naʿt of كنز. ﴿وَكانَ﴾: conjoined to the first كان. ﴿أَبُوهُما﴾: the noun of كان, nominative (marfūʿ) by the wāw because it is one of the five nouns, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿صالِحاً﴾: the khabar of كان. ﴿فَأَرادَ﴾: the fāʾ is linking, and a past verb. ﴿رَبُّكَ﴾: fāʿil (agent), and the kāf is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿أَنْ﴾: a particle governing the accusative. ﴿يَبْلُغا﴾: an imperfect verb in the accusative (manṣūb), the sign of its accusative being the dropping of the nūn because it is one of the five verbs; the alif of the dual is the fāʿil. ﴿أَشُدَّهُما﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi; the maṣdar is mafʿūl bihi. ﴿وَيَسْتَخْرِجا﴾: conjoined (maʿṭūf) to يبلغا, and its i'rab is like it. ﴿كَنزَهُما﴾: mafʿūl bihi, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿رَحْمَةً﴾: mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose). ﴿مِنْ رَبِّكَ﴾: the two are attached to رحمة. ﴿وَما﴾: the wāw is resumptive and ما is negative. ﴿فَعَلْتُهُ﴾: a past verb; the tāʾ is its fāʿil and the hāʾ is its object; the clause is resumptive. ﴿عَنْ أَمْرِي﴾: the two are attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿ذلِكَ﴾: ذا is a demonstrative in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ; the lām is for distance and the kāf is for address. ﴿تَأْوِيلُ﴾: khabar; the clause is resumptive. ﴿ما﴾: a relative noun in the position of the genitive by annexation. ﴿لَمْ﴾: a particle of the jussive, negation and conversion (qalb). ﴿تَسْطِعْ﴾: an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm), its fāʿil latent; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿عَلَيْهِ﴾: the two are attached to صبرا. ﴿صَبْراً﴾: mafʿūl bihi, accusative. ﴿وَيَسْئَلُونَكَ﴾: the wāw is resumptive, and an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn because it is one of the five verbs; the wāw is its fāʿil and the kāf is its object; the clause is resumptive. ﴿عَنْ﴾: a preposition. ﴿ذِي﴾: a genitive noun, the sign of its genitive being the yāʾ because it is one of the five nouns. ﴿الْقَرْنَيْنِ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr) by the yāʾ because it is dual. ﴿قُلْ﴾: an imperative verb whose fāʿil is latent; the clause is resumptive. ﴿سَأَتْلُوا﴾: the sīn is for the future, and an imperfect verb, nominative by an implied (muqaddar) ḍamma on the wāw owing to heaviness; its fāʿil is latent. ﴿عَلَيْكُمْ﴾: the two are attached to أتلو. ﴿مِنْهُ﴾: the two are attached to an omitted ḥāl of ذكرا. ﴿ذِكْراً﴾: mafʿūl bihi; the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl).

daas-irab:84-87.t: ﴿إِنَّا﴾: inna, and نا is its noun. ﴿مَكَّنَّا﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is the khabar (predicate) of inna. ﴿لَهُ﴾: the two are attached (mutaʿalliq) to مكنا. ﴿فِي الْأَرْضِ﴾: the two are attached to مكنا. ﴿وَآتَيْناهُ﴾: the wāw is conjunctive, and a past verb and its fāʿil, and the hāʾ is mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿مِنْ كُلِّ﴾: the two are attached to سببا. ﴿شَيْءٍ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive. ﴿سَبَباً﴾: mafʿūl bihi. ﴿فَأَتْبَعَ﴾: the fāʾ is conjunctive, and a past verb whose fāʿil is latent (mustatir). ﴿سَبَباً﴾: mafʿūl bihi. ﴿حَتَّى﴾: a particle of limit and a preposition. ﴿إِذا﴾: an adverb for future time, containing the sense of condition; the clause is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿بَلَغَ﴾: a past verb whose fāʿil is latent, its implied form being "هو". ﴿مَغْرِبَ﴾: mafʿūl bihi. ﴿الشَّمْسِ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَجَدَها﴾: a past verb whose fāʿil is latent, and the hāʾ is mafʿūl bihi; the clause has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition. ﴿تَغْرُبُ﴾: an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent; the clause is mafʿūl bihi of وجد. ﴿فِي عَيْنٍ﴾: the two are attached to تغرب. ﴿حَمِئَةٍ﴾: a naʿt (adjective). ﴿وَوَجَدَ﴾: the wāw is conjunctive, and a past verb whose fāʿil is latent. ﴿عِنْدَها﴾: an adverb of place attached to وجد, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿قَوْماً﴾: mafʿūl bihi. ﴿قُلْنا﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is resumptive. ﴿يا ذَا﴾: يا is a vocative particle, and ذا is the one addressed (munādā), annexed (muḍāf), accusative (manṣūb) by the alif because it is one of the five nouns. ﴿الْقَرْنَيْنِ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr) by the yāʾ because it is dual; the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿إِمَّا﴾: a particle of condition and detailing (tafṣīl). ﴿أَنْ﴾: a particle governing the accusative. ﴿تُعَذِّبَ﴾: an imperfect verb in the accusative; the fāʿil is latent; the interpreted maṣdar is in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), its khabar omitted. ﴿وَإِمَّا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and إما is a particle of condition and detailing. ﴿أَنْ تَتَّخِذَ﴾: أن is a particle governing the accusative, and an imperfect verb in the accusative whose fāʿil is latent. ﴿فِيهِمْ﴾: the two are attached to the verb تتخذ. ﴿حُسْناً﴾: mafʿūl bihi. ﴿قالَ﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil, latent; the clause is resumptive. ﴿أَمَّا﴾: a particle of condition and detailing. ﴿مَنْ﴾: a relative noun, mubtadaʾ. ﴿ظَلَمَ﴾: a past verb whose fāʿil is latent; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿فَسَوْفَ﴾: the fāʾ links the apodosis, and سوف is a particle of the future. ﴿نُعَذِّبُهُ﴾: an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent, and the hāʾ is mafʿūl bihi; the clause is the khabar of من. ﴿ثُمَّ﴾: a conjunction. ﴿يُرَدُّ﴾: a passive imperfect verb, and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is latent. ﴿إِلى رَبِّهِ﴾: the two are attached to يرد. ﴿فَيُعَذِّبُهُ﴾: the fāʾ is conjunctive, and an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ); the fāʿil is latent and the hāʾ is mafʿūl bihi. ﴿عَذاباً﴾: mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object). ﴿نُكْراً﴾: a naʿt.

daas-irab:88-95.t:
﴿وَأَمَّا﴾: conjoined to the preceding أما. ﴿مَنْ﴾: a relative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿آمَنَ﴾: a past verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause), with no grammatical position. ﴿وَعَمِلَ﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and a past verb whose fāʿil is latent. ﴿صالِحاً﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿فَلَهُ﴾: the fāʾ links the apodosis, and له: the two are attached (mutaʿalliq) to the fronted khabar (predicate). ﴿جَزاءً﴾: tamyīz (specification), accusative. ﴿الْحُسْنى﴾: a postponed mubtadaʾ, nominative (marfūʿ) by an implied (muqaddar) ḍamma on the alif owing to impossibility. ﴿وَسَنَقُولُ﴾: the wāw is conjunctive, and an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent. ﴿لَهُ﴾: the two are attached to نقول. ﴿مِنْ أَمْرِنا﴾: the two are attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), and نا is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿يُسْراً﴾: second mafʿūl bihi. ﴿ثُمَّ أَتْبَعَ سَبَباً﴾: its i'rab has passed shortly before. ﴿حَتَّى﴾: a particle of limit and a preposition. ﴿إِذا﴾: an adverb for future time, containing the sense of condition. ﴿بَلَغَ﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿مَطْلِعَ﴾: mafʿūl bihi. ﴿الشَّمْسِ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi; the clause is in the position of the genitive by annexation. ﴿وَجَدَها﴾: a past verb whose fāʿil is latent, and the hāʾ is mafʿūl bihi; the clause has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition. ﴿تَطْلُعُ﴾: an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent; the clause is the second mafʿūl bihi. ﴿عَلى قَوْمٍ﴾: the two are attached to تطلع. ﴿لَمْ نَجْعَلْ﴾: لم governs the jussive, and an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm); the fāʿil is latent; the clause is a naʿt (adjective) of قوم. ﴿لَهُمْ﴾: the two are attached to نجعل. ﴿مِنْ دُونِها﴾: the two are attached to an omitted ḥāl, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿سِتْراً﴾: mafʿūl bihi. ﴿كَذلِكَ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun, khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "الأمر كذلك"; the lām is for distance, the kāf is for address, and ذا is a demonstrative. ﴿وَقَدْ﴾: the wāw is conjunctive; قد is a particle of realisation (taḥqīq). ﴿أَحَطْنا﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿بِما﴾: the bāʾ is a preposition, and ما is a relative noun in the position of the genitive by the preposition; the two are attached to أحطنا. ﴿لَدَيْهِ﴾: an adverb of place attached to an omitted ṣila, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿خُبْراً﴾: mafʿūl bihi. ﴿ثُمَّ﴾: a conjunction. ﴿أَتْبَعَ﴾: a past verb whose fāʿil is latent. ﴿سَبَباً﴾: mafʿūl bihi; the clause is conjoined.
﴿حَتَّى﴾: a particle of limit and a preposition. ﴿إِذا﴾: an adverb for future time, containing the sense of condition. ﴿بَلَغَ﴾: a past verb, its fāʿil latent. ﴿بَيْنَ﴾: an adverb of place attached to بلغ. ﴿السَّدَّيْنِ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr) by the yāʾ. ﴿وَجَدَ﴾: a past verb whose fāʿil is latent; the clause is the apodosis. ﴿مِنْ دُونِهِما﴾: the two are attached to وجد, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿قَوْماً﴾: mafʿūl bihi. ﴿لا يَكادُونَ﴾: لا is negative, and an incomplete (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn; the wāw is in the position of the nominative as its noun; the clause is a naʿt of قوما. ﴿يَفْقَهُونَ﴾: an imperfect verb, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is the khabar of يكادون. ﴿قَوْلًا﴾: mafʿūl bihi. ﴿قالُوا﴾: a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma because it is attached to the wāw of the plural, and the wāw is the fāʿil. ﴿يا ذَا﴾: يا is a vocative particle, and ذا is the one addressed (munādā), accusative (manṣūb), the sign of its accusative being the alif because it is one of the five nouns. ﴿الْقَرْنَيْنِ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi, genitive by the yāʾ because it is dual. ﴿إِنَّ﴾: a particle resembling the verb. ﴿يَأْجُوجَ﴾: its noun. ﴿وَمَأْجُوجَ﴾: a noun conjoined (maʿṭūf) to يأجوج. ﴿مُفْسِدُونَ﴾: the khabar of inna, nominative by the wāw because it is a sound masculine plural. ﴿فِي الْأَرْضِ﴾: the two are attached to مفسدون; the vocative clause and what follows it are the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿فَهَلْ﴾: the fāʾ is conjunctive. ﴿هل﴾: an interrogative particle. ﴿نَجْعَلُ﴾: an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent. ﴿لَكَ﴾: the two are attached to نجعل. ﴿خَرْجاً﴾: mafʿūl bihi; the clause is conjoined. ﴿عَلى﴾: a preposition. ﴿إِنَّ﴾ [Translator's note: so in the source; the Quranic word here is ﴿أَنْ﴾, as the following «accusative by أن» shows.]: a particle governing the accusative. ﴿تَجْعَلَ﴾: an imperfect verb, accusative by an, its fāʿil latent; على and what follows it are attached to تجعل. ﴿بَيْنَنا﴾: an adverb of place attached to تجعل, and نا is an attached pronoun in the position of the genitive by annexation. ﴿وَبَيْنَهُمْ﴾: conjoined to بيننا. ﴿سَدًّا﴾: mafʿūl bihi. ﴿قالَ﴾: a past verb whose fāʿil is latent; the clause is resumptive. ﴿ما﴾: a relative noun, mubtadaʾ. ﴿مَكَّنِّي﴾: a past verb, indeclinable on the fatḥa; the nūn is the nūn of protection (wiqāya) and the yāʾ is mafʿūl bihi; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿فِيهِ﴾: the two are attached to مكني. ﴿رَبِّي﴾: fāʿil, nominative by an implied ḍamma on the letter before the yāʾ of the speaker, whose appearance is prevented by the place being occupied with the vowel suited to the yāʾ; the yāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿خَيْرٌ﴾: the khabar of ما. ﴿فَأَعِينُونِي﴾: the fāʾ is resumptive, and an imperative verb, indeclinable on the dropping of the nūn because it is attached to the wāw of the plural; the wāw is the fāʿil, the nūn is the nūn of protection and the yāʾ is mafʿūl bihi; the clause is resumptive. ﴿بِقُوَّةٍ﴾: the two are attached to أعينوني. ﴿أَجْعَلْ﴾: an imperfect verb, jussive because it is the response to the request (jawāb al-ṭalab), its fāʿil latent. ﴿بَيْنَكُمْ﴾: an adverb of place attached to أجعل, and the kāf is in the position of the genitive by annexation. ﴿وَبَيْنَهُمْ﴾: an adverb of place conjoined to بينكم. ﴿رَدْماً﴾: mafʿūl bihi.

daas-irab:96-98.t: ﴿آتُونِي﴾: an imperative verb; the wāw of the plural is the fāʿil (agent), the nūn is the nūn of protection (wiqāya), and the yāʾ is in the position of the accusative as the first mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿زُبَرَ﴾: second mafʿūl bihi, accusative. ﴿الْحَدِيدِ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause is resumptive. ﴿حَتَّى﴾: a particle of limit and a preposition. ﴿إِذا﴾: an adverb for future time, containing the sense of condition. ﴿ساوى﴾: a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on an implied (muqaddar) fatḥa on the alif owing to impossibility; its fāʿil is latent (mustatir); the clause is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿بَيْنَ﴾: an adverb of place attached (mutaʿalliq) to ساوى. ﴿الصَّدَفَيْنِ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi, genitive (majrūr) by the yāʾ because it is dual. ﴿قالَ﴾: a past verb whose fāʿil is latent; the clause is the response to إذا. ﴿انْفُخُوا﴾: an imperative verb, indeclinable on the dropping of the nūn because it is attached to the wāw of the plural; the wāw is the fāʿil. ﴿حَتَّى﴾: a particle of limit and a preposition. ﴿إِذا﴾: an adverb for future time, containing the sense of condition. ﴿جَعَلَهُ﴾: a past verb whose fāʿil is latent, and the hāʾ is the first mafʿūl bihi; the clause is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿ناراً﴾: second mafʿūl bihi. ﴿قالَ﴾: a past verb whose fāʿil is latent; the clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a non-jussive condition, with no grammatical position. ﴿آتُونِي﴾: its i'rab has passed shortly before; the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿أُفْرِغْ﴾: an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) because it is the response to the request (jawāb al-ṭalab); its fāʿil is latent, its implied form being "أنا". ﴿عَلَيْهِ﴾: the two are attached to أفرغ. ﴿قِطْراً﴾: mafʿūl bihi. ﴿فَمَا﴾: the fāʾ is conjunctive, and ما is negative, without governing effect. ﴿اسْطاعُوا﴾: a past verb, indeclinable on the ḍamma because it is attached to the wāw of the plural; the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause is conjoined. ﴿أَنْ﴾: a particle governing the accusative. ﴿يَظْهَرُوهُ﴾: an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an, the sign of its accusative being the dropping of the nūn because it is one of the five verbs; the wāw is the fāʿil and the hāʾ is mafʿūl bihi; the interpreted maṣdar is in the position of the accusative as mafʿūl bihi of اسطاعوا. ﴿وَمَا اسْتَطاعُوا﴾: conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it, and its i'rab is like it. ﴿لَهُ﴾: the two are attached to استطاعوا. ﴿نَقْباً﴾: mafʿūl bihi. ﴿قالَ﴾: a past verb whose fāʿil is latent; the clause is resumptive. ﴿هذا﴾: the hāʾ is for drawing attention (tanbīh), and ذا is a demonstrative, mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿رَحْمَةٌ﴾: khabar (predicate); the clause is the object of the saying. ﴿مِنْ رَبِّي﴾: the two are attached to an omitted naʿt (adjective), the implied form being "رحمة كائنة من ربي", and the yāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿فَإِذا﴾: the fāʾ is resumptive, and إذا is adverbial, conditional and non-jussive. ﴿جاءَ﴾: a past verb. ﴿وَعْدُ﴾: fāʿil; the clause is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿رَبِّي﴾: muḍāf ilayhi, and the yāʾ is in the position of the genitive by annexation. ﴿جَعَلَهُ﴾: a past verb, its fāʿil latent, and the hāʾ is the first mafʿūl bihi. ﴿دَكَّاءَ﴾: second mafʿūl bihi; the clause is the response to إذا. ﴿وَكانَ وَعْدُ﴾: the wāw is conjunctive, and kāna and its noun. ﴿رَبِّي﴾: muḍāf ilayhi, and the yāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿حَقًّا﴾: the khabar of kāna; the clause is conjoined.

daas-irab:99-102.t: ﴿وَتَرَكْنا﴾: the wāw is resumptive, and a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is resumptive. ﴿بَعْضَهُمْ﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿يَوْمَئِذٍ﴾: an adverb of time, and إذ is an adverb of time in the position of the genitive as muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿يَمُوجُ﴾: an imperfect verb; the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿فِي بَعْضٍ﴾: the two are attached (mutaʿalliq) to يموج. ﴿وَنُفِخَ﴾: the wāw is conjunctive, and a passive past verb whose nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is latent (mustatir). ﴿فِي الصُّورِ﴾: the two are attached to نفخ; the clause is conjoined. ﴿فَجَمَعْناهُمْ﴾: the fāʾ is conjunctive, and a past verb and its fāʿil, and the hāʾ is mafʿūl bihi. ﴿جَمْعاً﴾: mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object). ﴿وَعَرَضْنا﴾: the wāw is conjunctive, and a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿جَهَنَّمَ﴾: mafʿūl bihi. ﴿يَوْمَئِذٍ﴾: an adverb of time attached to عرضنا, and إذ is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿لِلْكافِرِينَ﴾: the two are attached to عرضنا. ﴿عَرْضاً﴾: mafʿūl muṭlaq. ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾: a relative noun, indeclinable (mabnī) on the fatḥa, in the position of the genitive as a naʿt (adjective) of الكافرين. ﴿كانَتْ أَعْيُنُهُمْ﴾: kāna and its noun, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿فِي غِطاءٍ﴾: the two are attached to the omitted khabar (predicate) of kāna. ﴿عَنْ ذِكْرِي﴾: the two are attached to an omitted naʿt of غطاء, and the yāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَكانُوا﴾: the wāw is conjunctive, and kāna and its noun; the clause is conjoined. ﴿لا يَسْتَطِيعُونَ﴾: لا is negative, and an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is the wāw of the plural; the clause is in the position of the accusative as the khabar of كانوا. ﴿سَمْعاً﴾: mafʿūl bihi. ﴿أَفَحَسِبَ الَّذِينَ﴾: the hamza is for interrogation, and a past verb, and the relative noun is the fāʿil. ﴿كَفَرُوا﴾: a past verb, indeclinable on the ḍamma because it is attached to the wāw of the plural; the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿أَنْ يَتَّخِذُوا﴾: أن is a particle governing the accusative, and an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an, the sign of its accusative being the dropping of the nūn because it is one of the five verbs; the wāw is in the position of the nominative as fāʿil; an and what follows it stand in place of the two objects of حسب. ﴿عِبادِي﴾: first mafʿūl bihi, and the yāʾ is in the position of the genitive by annexation. ﴿مِنْ دُونِي﴾: the two are attached to يتخذوا, and the yāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿أَوْلِياءَ﴾: second mafʿūl bihi. ﴿إِنَّا﴾: a particle resembling the verb, and نا is its noun; the clause is resumptive. ﴿أَعْتَدْنا﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the khabar. ﴿جَهَنَّمَ﴾: mafʿūl bihi. ﴿لِلْكافِرِينَ﴾: the two are attached to أعتدنا. ﴿نُزُلًا﴾: second mafʿūl bihi.

daas-irab:103-106.t: ﴿قُلْ﴾: an imperative verb, and the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is resumptive. ﴿هَلْ﴾: an interrogative particle. ﴿نُنَبِّئُكُمْ﴾: an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent, and the kāf is mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿بِالْأَخْسَرِينَ﴾: the two are attached (mutaʿalliq) to ننبئكم. ﴿أَعْمالًا﴾: tamyīz (specification). ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾: a relative noun in the position of the nominative as khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being "هم". ﴿ضَلَّ﴾: a past verb. ﴿سَعْيُهُمْ﴾: fāʿil, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿فِي الْحَياةِ﴾: the two are attached to ضل. ﴿الدُّنْيا﴾: a naʿt (adjective) of حياة, genitive by an implied (muqaddar) kasra on the alif. ﴿وَهُمْ﴾: the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāliyya), and هم is a detached pronoun in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ. ﴿يَحْسَبُونَ﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is the khabar, and the nominal clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿أَنَّهُمْ﴾: a particle resembling the verb, and the hāʾ is its noun; anna, its noun and its khabar stand in place of the two objects of يحسبون. ﴿يُحْسِنُونَ﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause is the khabar of anna. ﴿صُنْعاً﴾: mafʿūl bihi. ﴿أُولئِكَ﴾: a demonstrative in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ, and the kāf is for address. ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾: a relative noun in the position of the nominative as khabar. ﴿كَفَرُوا﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿بِآياتِ﴾: the two are attached to كفروا. ﴿رَبِّهِمْ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi, and the hāʾ is in the position of the genitive by annexation. ﴿وَلِقائِهِ﴾: a noun conjoined (maʿṭūf) by the wāw to what precedes it, genitive like it. ﴿فَحَبِطَتْ﴾: the fāʾ is conjunctive, and a past verb, and the tāʾ is for the feminine; the clause is conjoined. ﴿أَعْمالُهُمْ﴾: fāʿil, and the hāʾ is in the position of the genitive by annexation. ﴿فَلا﴾: the fāʾ is conjunctive and لا is negative. ﴿نُقِيمُ﴾: an imperfect verb, and the fāʿil is latent. ﴿لَهُمْ﴾: the two are attached to نقيم. ﴿يَوْمَ﴾: an adverb of time attached to نقيم. ﴿الْقِيامَةِ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَزْناً﴾: mafʿūl bihi. ﴿ذلِكَ﴾: a demonstrative in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ; the lām is for distance and the kāf is for address. ﴿جَزاؤُهُمْ﴾: mubtadaʾ, and the hāʾ is in the position of the genitive by annexation. ﴿جَهَنَّمُ﴾: khabar; the clause of mubtadaʾ and khabar is in the position of the nominative as khabar of the first mubtadaʾ, ذلك. ﴿بِما﴾: the bāʾ is a preposition, and ما is a relative noun in the position of the genitive by the preposition; the two are attached to جزاؤهم. ﴿كَفَرُوا﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿وَاتَّخَذُوا﴾: the wāw is conjunctive, and a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma because it is attached to the wāw of the plural; the wāw is in the position of the nominative as fāʿil; the clause is conjoined. ﴿آياتِي﴾: first mafʿūl bihi, and the yāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَرُسُلِي﴾: a noun conjoined to آياتي. ﴿هُزُواً﴾: second mafʿūl bihi.

daas-irab:107-109.t: ﴿إِنَّ﴾: a particle resembling the verb. ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾: a relative noun in the position of the accusative as the noun of inna. ﴿آمَنُوا﴾: a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on the ḍamma, and the wāw is the fāʿil (agent); the clause آمنوا is the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative, with no grammatical position. ﴿وَعَمِلُوا﴾: conjoined to آمنوا. ﴿الصَّالِحاتِ﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object), accusative (manṣūb) by the kasra in place of the fatḥa because it is a sound feminine plural. ﴿كانَتْ﴾: an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb, and the tāʾ is the tāʾ of the feminine; the clause is the khabar (predicate). ﴿لَهُمْ﴾: the two are attached (mutaʿalliq) to the khabar نزلا. ﴿جَنَّاتُ﴾: the noun of kāna. ﴿الْفِرْدَوْسِ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿نُزُلًا﴾: the khabar of kāna. ﴿خالِدِينَ﴾: ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative by the yāʾ because it is a sound masculine plural. ﴿فِيها﴾: the two are attached to خالدين. ﴿لا يَبْغُونَ﴾: لا is negative, and an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn; the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause is a ḥāl. ﴿عَنْها﴾: the two are attached to يبغون. ﴿حِوَلًا﴾: mafʿūl bihi. ﴿قُلْ﴾: an imperative verb whose fāʿil is latent (mustatir); the clause is resumptive. ﴿لَوْ﴾: a non-jussive conditional particle. ﴿كانَ الْبَحْرُ مِداداً﴾: kāna, its noun and its khabar; the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿لِكَلِماتِ﴾: the two are attached to مدادا. ﴿رَبِّي﴾: muḍāf ilayhi, and the yāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿لَنَفِدَ﴾: the lām occurs in the apodosis of the condition; the clause has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ). ﴿الْبَحْرُ﴾: fāʿil. ﴿قَبْلَ﴾: an adverb of time. ﴿أَنْ تَنْفَدَ﴾: أن is a particle governing the accusative, and an imperfect verb in the accusative. ﴿كَلِماتُ﴾: fāʿil. ﴿رَبِّي﴾: muḍāf ilayhi, and the yāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَلَوْ﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and لو is a non-jussive conditional particle. ﴿جِئْنا﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿بِمِثْلِهِ﴾: the two are attached to جئنا. ﴿مَدَداً﴾: mafʿūl bihi.

daas-irab:110-110.t: ﴿قُلْ﴾: an imperative verb, and the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is resumptive. ﴿إِنَّما﴾: restraining and restrained (kāffa wa-makfūfa). ﴿أَنَا بَشَرٌ﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate); the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿مِثْلُكُمْ﴾: a naʿt (adjective) of بشر. ﴿يُوحى﴾: a passive imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by an implied (muqaddar) ḍamma on the alif owing to impossibility; the clause is a naʿt of بشر. ﴿إِلَيَّ﴾: the two are attached (mutaʿalliq) to يوحى. ﴿إِنَّما﴾: restraining and restrained. ﴿إِلهُكُمْ﴾: mubtadaʾ, and the kāf is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿إِلهٌ﴾: khabar. ﴿واحِدٌ﴾: a naʿt; the clause is in the position of the nominative as nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent). ﴿فَمَنْ﴾: the fāʾ is resumptive, and من is a conditional noun governing the jussive, in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ. ﴿كانَ﴾: an incomplete (nāqiṣ) past verb whose noun is omitted. ﴿يَرْجُوا﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative by an implied ḍamma on the wāw owing to heaviness; the fāʿil is latent; the clause is the khabar. ﴿لِقاءَ﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿رَبِّهِ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿فَلْيَعْمَلْ﴾: the fāʾ links the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), the lām is the lām of command, and an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by the lām of command; the fāʿil is latent. ﴿عَمَلًا﴾: mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object). ﴿صالِحاً﴾: a naʿt of عمل, accusative. ﴿وَلا يُشْرِكْ﴾: the wāw is conjunctive and لا is prohibitive, and an imperfect verb in the jussive; the fāʿil is latent; the clause is conjoined. ﴿بِعِبادَةِ﴾: the two are attached to يشرك. ﴿رَبِّهِ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿أَحَداً﴾: mafʿūl bihi.

daas-irab:1-4.t: ﴿الْحَمْدُ﴾: mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿لِلَّهِ﴾: the Divine Name, genitive (majrūr) by the lām; the two are attached (mutaʿalliq) to the omitted khabar (predicate), and the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya). ﴿الَّذِي﴾: a relative noun, an adjective (ṣifa) of لله. ﴿أَنْزَلَ﴾: a past verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir). ﴿عَلى عَبْدِهِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أنزل. ﴿الْكِتابَ﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿وَلَمْ﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and lam puts the verb in the jussive. ﴿يَجْعَلْ﴾: an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent. ﴿لَهُ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يجعل. ﴿عِوَجاً﴾: mafʿūl bihi, and the clause is conjoined. ﴿قَيِّماً﴾: ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿لِيُنْذِرَ﴾: the lām is the lām of cause (taʿlīl), and an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied an after the lām of cause, and its fāʿil is latent; the lām and what follows it are attached to أنزل. ﴿بَأْساً﴾: second mafʿūl bihi. ﴿شَدِيداً﴾: an adjective. ﴿مِنْ لَدُنْهُ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ينذر, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿وَيُبَشِّرَ﴾: an imperfect verb, accusative, whose fāʿil is latent. ﴿الْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾: mafʿūl bihi, and the clause is conjoined. ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾: a relative noun in the position of the accusative as an adjective. ﴿يَعْمَلُونَ الصَّالِحاتِ﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn, and its fāʿil is the wāw, and الصالحات is its object, accusative by the kasra because it is a sound feminine plural; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿أَنَّ لَهُمْ أَجْراً﴾: anna and its postponed noun, and لهم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to the fronted khabar. ﴿حَسَناً﴾: an adjective; anna and what follows it are in the position of the accusative as the second mafʿūl bihi of يبشر. ﴿ماكِثِينَ﴾: ḥāl. ﴿فِيهِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ماكثين. ﴿أَبَداً﴾: an adverb of time, also attached to it. ﴿وَيُنْذِرَ﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent; the clause is conjoined. ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾: a relative noun, mafʿūl bihi. ﴿قالُوا﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is the ṣila. ﴿اتَّخَذَ اللَّهُ وَلَداً﴾: a past verb, and the Divine Name is its fāʿil, and ولدا is its object; the clause is the speech reported (maqūl al-qawl).

daas-irab:5-7.t: ﴿ما لَهُمْ﴾: mā is negative, and لهم is a preposition and its genitive noun attached (mutaʿalliq) to an omitted fronted khabar (predicate). ﴿بِهِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to علم. ﴿مِنْ﴾: a redundant (zāʾida) preposition. ﴿عِلْمٍ﴾: a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject), genitive in form and nominative in position; the clause is resumptive. ﴿وَلا﴾: the wāw is a conjunction; lā is redundant. ﴿لِآبائِهِمْ﴾: the two (preposition and noun) are conjoined to لهم. ﴿كَبُرَتْ﴾: a past verb for expressing blame, and the fāʿil (agent) is omitted, referring back to the word of disbelief. ﴿كَلِمَةً﴾: tamyīz (specification), and the clause is resumptive. ﴿تَخْرُجُ﴾: an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent (mustatir), and the clause is an adjective (ṣifa) of كلمة. ﴿مِنْ أَفْواهِهِمْ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to تخرج. ﴿إِنْ﴾: a particle of negation. ﴿يَقُولُونَ﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil. ﴿إِلَّا﴾: a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). ﴿كَذِباً﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the clause is resumptive. ﴿فَلَعَلَّكَ﴾: the fāʾ is resumptive; laʿalla and its noun. ﴿باخِعٌ﴾: khabar. ﴿نَفْسَكَ﴾: mafʿūl bihi of باخع, and the kāf is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿عَلى آثارِهِمْ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to باخع. ﴿إِنْ﴾: conditional. ﴿لَمْ﴾: puts the verb in the jussive. ﴿يُؤْمِنُوا﴾: an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by the deletion of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya) and has no grammatical position. ﴿بِهذَا﴾: the hā is for drawing attention, and ذا is a demonstrative; the two are attached to يؤمنوا. ﴿الْحَدِيثِ﴾: badal (substitute) or ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition). ﴿أَسَفاً﴾: mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose); the apodosis of the condition is omitted because what precedes it indicates it. ﴿إِنَّا﴾: inna and its noun, and the clause is resumptive. ﴿جَعَلْنا﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is the khabar. ﴿ما﴾: a relative noun, mafʿūl bihi. ﴿عَلَى الْأَرْضِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ṣila (relative clause). ﴿زِينَةً﴾: second mafʿūl bihi or mafʿūl li-ajlihi. ﴿لَها﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to زينة. ﴿لِنَبْلُوَهُمْ﴾: the lām is the lām of cause (taʿlīl), and an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied an after the lām of cause, and its fāʿil is latent, and the hāʾ is mafʿūl bihi; the lām and what follows it are attached to جعلنا. ﴿أَيُّهُمْ﴾: an interrogative noun, mubtadaʾ, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿أَحْسَنُ﴾: khabar. ﴿عَمَلًا﴾: tamyīz, and the clause takes the place of the two objects of نبلوهم.

daas-irab:8-11.t: ﴿وَإِنَّا لَجاعِلُونَ﴾: inna, its noun and its khabar (predicate), and the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); the clause is conjoined. ﴿ما﴾: mā is a relative noun, mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of جاعلون. ﴿عَلَيْها﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached (mutaʿalliq) to an omitted ṣila (relative clause). ﴿صَعِيداً﴾: second mafʿūl bihi. ﴿جُرُزاً﴾: an adjective (ṣifa). ﴿أَمْ﴾: a conjunction. ﴿حَسِبْتَ﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil (agent), and the clause is resumptive. ﴿أَنَّ أَصْحابَ﴾: anna and its noun. ﴿الْكَهْفِ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿وَالرَّقِيمِ﴾: maʿṭūf (conjoined) to الكهف; the interpreted maṣdar (verbal noun) takes the place of the two objects of حسب. ﴿كانُوا﴾: kāna and its noun. ﴿مِنْ آياتِنا﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to عجبا; نا is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿عَجَباً﴾: the khabar of كانوا, and the clause is the khabar of inna [Translator's note: i.e. of anna]. ﴿إِذْ﴾: an adverb. ﴿أَوَى الْفِتْيَةُ﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿إِلَى الْكَهْفِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أوى. ﴿فَقالُوا﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction, and a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿رَبَّنا﴾: the one addressed (munādā) with an omitted vocative particle; it is accusative (manṣūb) as a vocative, and نا is muḍāf ilayhi; the clause is the speech reported (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿آتِنا﴾: a verb of supplication whose fāʿil is latent (mustatir), and نا is the first mafʿūl bihi; the clause is the speech reported. ﴿مِنْ لَدُنْكَ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to آتنا, and the kāf is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿رَحْمَةً﴾: second mafʿūl bihi. ﴿وَهَيِّئْ﴾: conjoined to آتنا, and its fāʿil is latent. ﴿لَنا﴾ and ﴿مِنْ أَمْرِنا﴾: both are attached to هيئ. ﴿رَشَداً﴾: mafʿūl bihi. ﴿فَضَرَبْنا﴾: the fāʾ is a conjunction, and a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is conjoined. ﴿عَلَى آذانِهِمْ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ضربنا, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿فِي الْكَهْفِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ضربنا. ﴿سِنِينَ﴾: mafʿūl fīhi (adverbial), an adverb of time, accusative by the yāʾ because it is assimilated to the sound masculine plural. ﴿عَدَداً﴾: an adjective.

daas-irab:12-14.t: ﴿ثُمَّ﴾: a conjunction. ﴿بَعَثْناهُمْ﴾: a past verb, its fāʿil (agent) and its object, and the clause is conjoined. ﴿لِنَعْلَمَ﴾: the lām is the lām of cause (taʿlīl), and an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb) by an implied an after the lām of cause, and the fāʿil is latent (mustatir); the lām and what follows it are attached (mutaʿalliq) to بعثناهم. ﴿أَيُّ﴾: an interrogative noun, mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿الْحِزْبَيْنِ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct), genitive (majrūr) by the yāʾ because it is dual. ﴿أَحْصى﴾: a past verb, indeclinable (mabnī) on an implied (muqaddar) fatḥa on the alif because of impossibility, and the clause is in the position of the nominative as the khabar (predicate) of أي. ﴿لِما﴾: the lām is a preposition, and mā is a relative noun in the position of the genitive; the two are attached to أحصى. ﴿لَبِثُوا﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). ﴿أَمَداً﴾: tamyīz (specification). ﴿نَحْنُ﴾: mubtadaʾ, and the clause is resumptive. ﴿نَقُصُّ﴾: an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is a latent pronoun, and the clause is the khabar. ﴿عَلَيْكَ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to نقص. ﴿نَبَأَهُمْ﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿بِالْحَقِّ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿إِنَّهُمْ فِتْيَةٌ﴾: inna, its noun and its khabar, and the clause is resumptive. ﴿آمَنُوا﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is an adjective (ṣifa) of فتية. ﴿بِرَبِّهِمْ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to آمنوا. ﴿وَزِدْناهُمْ﴾: conjoined to آمنوا; a past verb, its fāʿil and its object. ﴿هُدىً﴾: tamyīz, accusative by an implied fatḥa on the alif because of impossibility, or second mafʿūl bihi of زدناهم. ﴿وَرَبَطْنا﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is conjoined. ﴿عَلى قُلُوبِهِمْ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ربطنا. ﴿إِذْ﴾: an adverb of time. ﴿قامُوا﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿فَقالُوا﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil, and the clause is conjoined. ﴿رَبُّنا﴾: mubtadaʾ, and نا is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿رَبُّ﴾: khabar, and the clause is the speech reported (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿السَّماواتِ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَالْأَرْضِ﴾: maʿṭūf (conjoined) to السموات. ﴿لَنْ﴾: puts the verb in the accusative. ﴿نَدْعُوَا﴾: an imperfect verb, accusative by lan. ﴿مِنْ دُونِهِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ندعو, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿إِلهاً﴾: mafʿūl bihi. ﴿لَقَدْ﴾: the lām occurs in the answer to an omitted oath, and قد is a particle of realisation (taḥqīq). ﴿قُلْنا﴾: a past verb and its fāʿil, and the clause has no grammatical position because it is the answer to an oath. ﴿إِذاً﴾: a particle of answer. ﴿شَطَطاً﴾: mafʿūl bihi, accusative.

daas-irab:15-16.t: ﴿هؤُلاءِ﴾: the hā is for drawing attention; أولاء is a demonstrative in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿قَوْمُنَا﴾: khabar (predicate), and نا is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause is resumptive. ﴿اتَّخَذُوا﴾: a past verb, and the wāw is its fāʿil (agent). ﴿مِنْ دُونِهِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached (mutaʿalliq) to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial), and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿آلِهَةً﴾: mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the clause is a ḥāl. ﴿لَوْلا﴾: a particle of urging (taḥḍīḍ). ﴿يَأْتُونَ﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil. ﴿عَلَيْهِمْ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يأتون. ﴿بِسُلْطانٍ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يأتون. ﴿بَيِّنٍ﴾: an adjective (ṣifa). ﴿فَمَنْ﴾: the fāʾ is resumptive, and من is an interrogative noun in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ. ﴿أَظْلَمُ﴾: khabar, and the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) [Translator's note: so in the source; من here is interrogative, and the clause is resumptive]. ﴿مِمَّنِ﴾: من is a relative noun in the position of the genitive, and the two are attached to أظلم. ﴿افْتَرى﴾: a past verb whose fāʿil is latent (mustatir). ﴿عَلَى اللَّهِ﴾: the Divine Name, genitive (majrūr) by على; the two are attached to افترى. ﴿كَذِباً﴾: mafʿūl bihi, and the clause is the ṣila of the relative noun. ﴿وَإِذِ﴾: the wāw is resumptive; إذ is an adverb of time attached to an omitted verb, its implied form being "اذكر" (remember). ﴿اعْتَزَلْتُمُوهُمْ﴾: a past verb, its fāʿil and its object, and the clause is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَما﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and mā is a relative noun. ﴿يَعْبُدُونَ﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative by the retention of the nūn, and the wāw is the fāʿil; the clause is conjoined. ﴿إِلَّا﴾: a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr). ﴿اللَّهَ﴾: the Divine Name, mafʿūl bihi. ﴿فَأْوُوا﴾: the fāʾ is al-faṣīḥa (signalling an implied condition), and an imperative verb and its fāʿil; the clause has no grammatical position. ﴿إِلَى الْكَهْفِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أووا. ﴿يَنْشُرْ﴾: an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) because it is the answer to the command. ﴿لَكُمْ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ينشر. ﴿رَبُّكُمْ﴾: fāʿil, and the kāf is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿مِنْ رَحْمَتِهِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ينشر, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَيُهَيِّئْ﴾: conjoined to ينشر. ﴿لَكُمْ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to يهيء. ﴿مِنْ أَمْرِكُمْ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to an omitted ḥāl, and the kāf is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿مِرفَقاً﴾: mafʿūl bihi.

daas-irab:17-18.t: ﴿وَتَرَى الشَّمْسَ﴾: the wāw is resumptive, and an imperfect verb, nominative (marfūʿ) by an implied (muqaddar) ḍamma on the alif because of impossibility, and its fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), and الشمس is its object; the clause is resumptive. ﴿إِذا﴾: an adverb of future time attached (mutaʿalliq) to its apodosis. ﴿طَلَعَتْ﴾: a past verb whose fāʿil is latent, the tāʾ being of the feminine, and the clause is muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct). ﴿تَتَزاوَرُ﴾: an imperfect verb, nominative, and its fāʿil is latent; the clause is the apodosis of the condition and has no grammatical position. ﴿عَنْ كَهْفِهِمْ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to تزاور, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿ذاتَ﴾: an adverb of place attached to تزاور. ﴿الْيَمِينِ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَإِذا غَرَبَتْ﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, and the clause غربت is muḍāf ilayhi; see the i'rab of إذا طلعت. ﴿تَقْرِضُهُمْ ذاتَ الشِّمالِ﴾: see the i'rab of تزاور عن كهفهم ذات اليمين; its i'rab is like it. ﴿وَهُمْ﴾: the wāw is of the ḥāl (circumstantial), and هم is mubtadaʾ (subject). ﴿فِي فَجْوَةٍ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to the khabar (predicate), and the clause is a ḥāl. ﴿ذلِكَ﴾: ذا is a demonstrative, mubtadaʾ, the lām is for distance and the kāf is for address. ﴿مِنْ آياتِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to the omitted khabar, and the clause is resumptive. ﴿اللَّهِ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿مِنْ﴾: conditional, in the position of the accusative as a fronted mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿يَهْدِ اللَّهُ فَهُوَ الْمُهْتَدِ﴾: an imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm) by the deletion of the weak letter, and the Divine Name is the fāʿil. ﴿فَهُوَ﴾: the fāʾ is linking, and هو is mubtadaʾ. ﴿الْمُهْتَدِ﴾: khabar, the yāʾ having been deleted for lightness; the clause is in the position of the jussive as the jawāb al-sharṭ (apodosis). ﴿وَمَنْ يُضْلِلْ فَلَنْ تَجِدَ﴾: its i'rab is similar to the i'rab of the preceding one; lan is a particle that puts the verb in the accusative, and تجد is an imperfect verb, accusative (manṣūb), and its fāʿil is latent; the clause is in the position of the jussive as the jawāb al-sharṭ. ﴿لَهُ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to تجد. ﴿وَلِيًّا﴾: mafʿūl bihi. ﴿مُرْشِداً﴾: an adjective (ṣifa). ﴿وَتَحْسَبُهُمْ أَيْقاظاً﴾: an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent, and its two objects, and the clause is conjoined. ﴿وَهُمْ رُقُودٌ﴾: the wāw is of the ḥāl, and mubtadaʾ and khabar; the clause is a ḥāl. ﴿وَنُقَلِّبُهُمْ﴾: an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent, and the hāʾ is its object; the clause is conjoined. ﴿ذاتَ﴾: an adverb of place attached to نقلبهم. ﴿الْيَمِينِ﴾: muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿وَذاتَ الشِّمالِ﴾: conjoined to what preceded, and its i'rab is like it. ﴿وَكَلْبُهُمْ باسِطٌ﴾: mubtadaʾ and khabar, and the clause is a ḥāl. ﴿ذِراعَيْهِ﴾: mafʿūl bihi of باسط, accusative by the yāʾ because it is dual, and the hāʾ is muḍāf ilayhi. ﴿بِالْوَصِيدِ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to باسط. ﴿لَوِ﴾: a non-jussive conditional particle. ﴿اطَّلَعْتَ﴾: a past verb whose fāʿil is latent, and the tāʾ is for the feminine [Translator's note: so in the source; the tāʾ here is the second-person pronoun and is the fāʿil]; the clause has no grammatical position. ﴿عَلَيْهِمْ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to اطلعت. ﴿لَوَلَّيْتَ﴾: the lām occurs in the apodosis of law, and a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause has no grammatical position because it is the apodosis of a non-jussive condition. ﴿مِنْهُمْ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to وليت. ﴿فِراراً﴾: a substitute for the mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), because ولّى means فرّ (to flee). ﴿وَلَمُلِئْتَ﴾: the wāw is a conjunction, the lām occurs in the apodosis of law, and a passive past verb, and the tāʾ is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); the clause is conjoined. ﴿مِنْهُمْ﴾: a preposition and its genitive noun attached to ملئت. ﴿رُعْباً﴾: tamyīz (specification).

farraa:1-5.t:
His saying, Blessed and Exalted: ﴿وَلَمْ يَجْعَل لَّهُ عِوَجَا قَيِّماً﴾ (and has not made in it any crookedness — straight): the meaning is: praise be to Allah who sent down the Book to His servant straight (قَيِّما), and has not made in it any crookedness. It is also said of القيّم: a guardian over the (other) scriptures, i.e. it confirms them.
His saying ﴿لِّيُنْذِرَ بَأْساً شَدِيداً﴾ (to warn of a severe punishment): along with "the punishment" there are suppressed nouns on which the verb falls before it falls on "the punishment". Similar is (the verse) in Āl ʿImrān: ﴿إنَّما ذَلِكُمُ الشَّيطَان يُخَوِّف أَوْلِيَاءَهُ﴾ (that is only Satan who frightens [you] of his allies); its meaning is: he frightens you of his allies.
His saying: ﴿مَّا لَهُمْ بِهِ مِنْ عِلْمٍ وَلاَ لآبَائِهِمْ﴾ (they have no knowledge of it, nor did their fathers): its meaning is: nor their forebears — their fathers and their fathers' fathers; [and not] meaning only the fathers who are their immediate begetters.
His saying: ﴿كَبُرَتْ كَلِمَةً تَخْرُجُ مِنْ أَفْوَاهِهِمْ﴾ (grave is the word that comes out of their mouths): the companions of ʿAbdallāh made it (كلمة) accusative, and al-Ḥasan and some of the people of Medina made it nominative. Whoever makes it accusative suppresses (a subject) in (كبرت): "that word is grave as a word". Whoever makes it nominative suppresses nothing; just as you say: "your statement is enormous, and your speech is grave".

farraa:10-10.t: His saying: ﴿وَهَيِّىءْ﴾ (and prepare): the hamza was written with alif — (وهَيَّأْ) — according to its spelling. The hamza is mostly written according to what precedes it: if what precedes it has fatḥa, it is written with alif; if ḍamma, it is written with wāw; and if kasra, it is written with yāʾ. Sometimes the Arabs wrote it with alif in every case, because its origin is alif. They said: we see that when it is initial it is written with alif whether it has fatḥa, kasra or ḍamma; as in your saying أُمِروا, أَمَرت, and ﴿وقد جئتَ شيئاً إمْرا﴾ (you have done a grievous thing); so they followed this approach. He said: I saw it in the codex of ʿAbdallāh (شيْأً), with alif in its nominative and genitive (forms), and I saw يستهزءون written يستهزأون with alif; and that is the analogical form. The first (way) is more common in the written copies.

farraa:11-11.t:
His saying: ﴿فَضَرَبْنَا عَلَىٰ آذَانِهِمْ﴾ (so We cast [a cover] over their ears): with sleep.
His saying: ﴿سِنِينَ عَدَداً﴾ (for a number of years): العَدَد here is in the sense of "counted" (معدودة), and Allah knows best. When what precedes العدد is a named number, like the hundred, the thousand, the ten and the five, there are two aspects for العدد. One is that you make it accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun), so you say: لك عندى عشرة عَدَداً (I owe you ten, by count); you derive "count" from "ten", because "ten" contains the meaning "they were counted", as though you said: they were reckoned and counted, by count (عَدَداً and عَدّا). And if you wish you make العدد nominative, meaning: you have ten counted (ones). So العدد here, with "years", is like His saying, Blessed and Exalted, in (Sūrat) Yūsuf: ﴿وَشَرَوْهُ بِثَمَنٍ بَخْسٍ دَرَاهِمَ مَعْدُودَةٍ﴾ (and they sold him for a paltry price, a few counted dirhams), because the dirhams are not named by a number. Likewise whatever is measured by volume or weight: you produce it (when it comes) after its names in the two ways. So you say: لك عندى عشرة أرطال وَزناً and وَزنٌ (I owe you ten raṭls by weight), and كيلاً and كيلٌ (by measure), on that basis.

farraa:12-12.t:
His saying: ﴿لِنَعْلَمَ أَيُّ الحِزْبَيْنِ أَحْصَىٰ﴾ (that We might make evident which of the two parties was more precise in reckoning): you make أىّ nominative by أحصى (i.e. as mubtadaʾ (subject) with أحصى as its khabar (predicate)), because "knowing" does not fall upon أىّ; it is only: "that you may know by looking and asking". It is like your saying: "go and find out for me which of them stood", for do you not see that you only make the knowing fall on the one from whom you seek information. What makes that clear is that you say: سَلْ عبدَالله أَيُّهم قامَ (ask ʿAbdallāh which of them stood); if you dropped ʿAbdallāh, you would still be intending him, or someone like him among those who give information.
His saying: ﴿أَيُّ الحِزْبَيْنِ﴾ (which of the two parties): it is said that two groups of Muslims in the time of the companions of the cave differed about their number. It is also said: the disbelievers and the Muslims differed. As for (أَحْصَىٰ), it is said: more correct, i.e. which of them spoke correctly.
His saying: ﴿أَمَداً﴾ (in period): أمدا may be accusative in two ways. If you wish, you make it derive from ﴿أَحْصَىٰ﴾ as a specifying explanation (tamyīz (specification)), as you say: "which of the two parties is more correct in speech"; and if you wish, you make the "staying" fall on it: for their staying a period.

farraa:16-16.t:
His saying: ﴿وَإِذِ ٱعْتَزَلْتُمُوهُمْ وَمَا يَعْبُدُونَ﴾ (and since you have withdrawn from them and what they worship) means the companions of the cave. He said: since you have withdrawn from all the gods they worship except Allah. (ما) is in the position of the accusative. That is because they used to associate partners with Allah, so He said: you have withdrawn from the idols, but you have not withdrawn from Allah, Blessed and Exalted, nor from His worship.
His saying: ﴿فَأْوُوا إِلَى ٱلْكَهْفِ﴾ (then take refuge in the cave) is the answer to إذْ, as you say: "since you have done what you did, then repent".
His saying: ﴿مِّنْ أَمْرِكُمْ مِّرْفَقاً﴾ (some ease in your affair): al-Aʿmash and al-Ḥasan gave the mīm kasra, and the people of Medina and ʿĀṣim gave it fatḥa. It seems that those who gave the mīm fatḥa and the fāʾ kasra wished to distinguish between المَرْفِق "of an affair" and المِرْفَق "of a person" (the elbow). Most of the Arabs give the mīm kasra both for the affair and for the person. The Arabs also give the mīm fatḥa in مرفق of a person. They are two dialect forms in both.

farraa:17-17.t: His saying: ﴿تَّزَاوَرُ﴾ (it inclines away): it has also been read ﴿تزَّاوَرُ﴾, meaning (تَتَزاور), the tāʾ being assimilated into the zāy. Some read (تَزْوَرّ) and some (تَزْوَارّ), like تَحْمرّ and تَحْمارّ. The inclining away (الازورار) here is that it (the sun) would rise upon their cave on the right side and not enter upon them, and (likewise) on the left side. The Arabs say: قرضته ذات اليمين (I passed it on the right) and حَذَوته (I was alongside it), and likewise ذات الشمال (on the left), قُبُلا (in front) and دُبُرا (behind) — all of that meaning: I was alongside it on every side.

farraa:18-18.t:
His saying: ﴿ذِرَاعَيْهِ بِٱلوَصِيدِ﴾ (its forelegs at the threshold): الوَصِيد is the courtyard (al-fināʾ). الوصيد and الأَصيد are two dialect forms, like الإكَاف and الوِكَاف (pack-saddle), and like أَرَّخْت الكتاب and وَرَّخته (I dated the letter), وكَّدت الأمر and أكَّدته (I confirmed the matter), and وضعْتُه يَتْنا, أَتْنا and وَتْنَا, meaning the child (born feet first). As for the Arabs' saying واخيت, وامرت, واتيت and واسيت, these are built on المواخاة, المواسَاة, المواتاة and الموامرة, and their origin is with hamza; just as it is said: هو سْوَل منك, whose origin is with hamza, and it was changed into wāw and built on السوَال.
His saying: ﴿فِي فَجْوَةٍ مِّنْهُ﴾ (in an open space thereof): i.e. a spacious area.
His saying: ﴿وَلَمُلِئْتَ﴾ (and you would have been filled): ʿĀṣim and al-Aʿmash read it with the light form, and the people of Medina read ﴿وَلَمُلِئْتَ مِنْهُمْ﴾ with the doubled form. «[Translator's note: both forms are quoted in the text with the same spelling; the doubled reading is لَمُلِّئْتَ.]» This is addressed to Muhammad ﷺ.

farraa:19-19.t:
His saying: ﴿بِوَرِقِكُمْ﴾ (with this silver coin of yours): ʿĀṣim and al-Aʿmash read it with the light form, and it is الوَرِق. Some Arabs say الوِرْق, just as one says كَبِد, كِبْدٌ and كَبْدٌ (liver), and كَلِمَةٌ, كَلْمَةٌ and كِلْمَة (word).
His saying ﴿فَلْيَنْظُرْ أَيُّهَآ أَزْكَىٰ﴾ (and let him see which of it is purest): it is said: which is the most lawful slaughtered meat, because they were Magians.

farraa:21-21.t: His saying: ﴿أَعْثَرْنَا عَلَيْهِمْ﴾ (We caused [them] to find them): We made (them) manifest and caused (them) to be discovered. Similar is (the verse) in al-Māʾida: ﴿فإن عُثِرَ﴾ (and if it is found): it is discovered. (The singular of الأيقاظ (awake) is يَقِظ and يَقُظ.) «[Translator's note: the text has "الأبقاظ".]»

farraa:22-22.t:
His saying: ﴿وَيَقُولُونَ سَبْعَةٌ وَثَامِنُهُمْ كَلْبُهُمْ﴾ (and they say: seven, and the eighth of them their dog): Ibn ʿAbbās said: they were seven, and the eighth of them was their dog. And Ibn ʿAbbās said: I am among the few of whom Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿مَّا يَعْلَمُهُمْ إِلاَّ قَلِيلٌ﴾ (none knows them except a few).
Then Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said to His Prophet, upon him be peace: ﴿فَلاَ تُمَارِ فِيهِمْ﴾ (so do not argue about them), O Muhammad, ﴿إِلاَّ مِرَآءً ظَاهِراً﴾ (except with an obvious argument): except that you tell them about it as a narration.
His saying: ﴿وَلاَ تَسْتَفْتِ فِيهِمْ﴾ (and do not inquire about them) — about the people of the cave — (مِّنْهُمْ) (among them) — of the Christians — (أَحَداً) (anyone). They were two parties who came to him from the people of Najrān: a Jacobite and a Nestorian. The Prophet ﷺ asked them about their number, and he was forbidden (to do so). That is His saying ﴿وَلاَ تَسْتَفْتِ فِيهِمْ مِّنْهُمْ أَحَداً﴾.

farraa:23-24.t:
His saying: ﴿وَلاَ تَقْولَنَّ لِشَيْءٍ إِنِّي فَاعِلٌ ذٰلِكَ غَداً﴾ (and never say of anything: "I shall do that tomorrow") ﴿إِلاَّ أَن يَشَآءَ ٱللَّهُ﴾ (except [adding]: "if Allah wills"): except that you say: "if Allah wills" (and, along with "saying", it may be: and do not say it unless Allah wills), i.e. except what Allah intends.
His saying ﴿وَٱذْكُر رَّبَّكَ إِذَا نَسِيتَ﴾ (and remember your Lord when you forget): Ibn ʿAbbās said: when you swear an oath and forget to make the exception (i.e. to say "if Allah wills"), make the exception whenever you remember, as long as you have not broken the oath.

farraa:25-25.t:
His saying: ﴿ثَلاثَ مِئَةٍ سِنِينَ﴾ (three hundred years) — in genitive construct. «[Translator's note: i.e. the reading ثلاثَ مئةِ سنين without nunation.]» Many readers read (ثَلاثَ مِئَةٍ سِنِينَ) (with nunation), meaning "and they stayed in their cave years", so they make it accusative by the verb.
Some Arabs put السنين in the place of سَنَة (year), and it is then in the position of the genitive for whoever uses the construct. Whoever nunates while meaning the construct sense makes السنين accusative as an explanation (tamyīz (specification)) of the number, like the saying of ʿAntara:
فيها اثنتان وَأربعونَ حَلُوبةً * سُودا كخافية الغُراب الأَسحم
(Among them are forty-two milch camels, black like the inner feathers of the jet-black raven.)
He made (سُوداً), which is a plural, a specification, just as the singular specifies.

farraa:26-26.t:
His saying: ﴿أَبْصِرْ بِهِ وَأَسْمِعْ﴾ (how Seeing is He, and how Hearing!): He means Allah, Blessed and Exalted, like your saying in ordinary speech: أكرم بعبدالله (how noble is ʿAbdallāh!), whose meaning is: ما أكرم عبدالله. Likewise His saying ﴿أَسْمِعْ بِهِمْ وَأَبْصِر﴾: how well they will hear, how well they will see! In anything that has a sense of praise or blame you say: أظرِف به (how witty he is!) and أكرم به; and from (roots with) yāʾ and wāw: أَطْيِبُ به طعاماً (how good it is as food!) and أجْوِد به ثوباً (how fine it is as a garment!). With doubled roots you show the doubling, and assimilation is not permitted, just as dropping the yāʾ or the wāw is not permitted, because its origin is ما أجوده, ما أشدّه and أطيبه, so it was left on that basis. As for أَشدِد به, the doubling appears because of the vowellessness of the lām (third radical) of the verb, and the doubling was kept and not assimilated because it is not put in the dual or feminine: you do not say to two أشِدَّا بِهما, nor to a group أَشِدُّوا بهم. The Arabs allowed themselves to say مدّ in place of امدد only because they say to two مُدَّا and to a group مُدُّوا, so the singular was built on the plural.
His saying ﴿وَلاَ يُشْرِكُ فِي حُكْمِهِ أَحَداً﴾ (and He shares His rule with no one): you make it nominative when it is with yāʾ, in the sense of "and He does not share". Whoever said ﴿لاَ تُشْرِكْ﴾ (do not associate) made it jussive (majzūm), because it is a prohibition.

farraa:27-28.t:
His saying: ﴿مُلْتَحَداً﴾ (a refuge): المُلْتَحد is the place of refuge.
His saying: ﴿بِٱلْغَدَاةِ وَٱلْعَشِيِّ﴾ (morning and evening): Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī read (بالغُدْوة والعَشِّى), and I know of no one who read it otherwise «[Translator's note: so the text; the sense is presumably that no one else read بالغدوة.]». The Arabs do not put the alif and lām (the definite article) on غدوة, because it is definite without alif and lām. I heard Abū al-Jarrāḥ say: "I have never seen anything like غُدْوةَ (this morning)", meaning the morning of his day, because it was cold. Do you not see that the Arabs do not put it in the construct; likewise they do not put alif and lām on it. They only say: أتيتكَ غَدَاة الخميس (I came to you on Thursday morning), and do not say: غُدْوةَ الخميس. This is evidence that it is definite.
His saying ﴿وَلاَ تَعْدُ عَيْنَاكَ عَنْهُمْ﴾ (and let not your eyes pass beyond them): the verb belongs to the eyes: let your eyes not turn away from them. This was revealed concerning Salmān and his companions.
His saying ﴿وَكَانَ أَمْرُهُ فُرُطاً﴾ (and whose affair is ever neglect): neglected, obedience having been abandoned in it and disregarded. It is also said that he went to excess in speech, saying: "We are the heads of Muḍar and its nobles", and it was not so. He is ʿUyayna ibn Ḥiṣn. We have mentioned his story in Sūrat al-Anʿām.

farraa:30-30.t:
His saying: ﴿إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ وَعَمِلُواْ ٱلصَّالِحَاتِ إِنَّا لاَ نُضِيعُ﴾ (indeed those who believed and did righteous deeds — indeed We will not allow to be lost): the khabar (predicate) of ﴿ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ﴾ is in His saying ﴿إِنَّا لاَ نُضِيعُ﴾. It is like the saying of the poet:
إِن الخليفة إنَّ الله سَرْبله * سِرْبالَ مُلْك بها تُزْجَى الخواتيمُ
(Indeed the caliph — indeed Allah has clothed him in the garment of kingship, by which seals are dispatched.)
It is as though, in meaning: "indeed We will not allow to be lost the reward of whoever did good"; so the first statement was left and reliance placed on the second, with the intention of repetition; as He said ﴿يَسْأَلُونَكَ عَنِ الشَّهْرِ الحَرَامِ﴾ (they ask you about the sacred month), then said ﴿قِتَالٍ فيهِ﴾ (fighting in it), meaning "about fighting in it", by repetition. It may also be that you take ﴿إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُواْ وَعَمِلُواْ﴾ in the manner of a condition (jazāʾ), as you say: "indeed whoever does good, then We will not allow his reward to be lost", so you suppress — «[Translator's note: the text has "ب: فتضمر فتضمَّن", i.e. manuscript B reads فتضمر where the main text has فتضمَّن.]» — the fāʾ in His saying (فإنَّا), and dropping it is permitted. That is the aspect dearest to me. And if you wish you make their khabar come later, as though you said: ﴿إن الذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات أولئك لهم جَنَّات عَدْن﴾ (indeed those who believed and did righteous deeds — those will have gardens of perpetual residence).

farraa:6-6.t:
His saying: ﴿فَلَعَلَّكَ بَاخِعٌ نَّفْسَكَ﴾ (perhaps you would kill yourself [with grief]): i.e. one who takes your own life out, one who kills himself.
His saying: ﴿إِن لَّمْ يُؤْمِنُواْ﴾ (if they do not believe): you give it kasra when they have not yet believed, with the intention of a condition (jazāʾ); and you give it fatḥa when you mean that it has already happened; like His saying elsewhere: ﴿أَفَنَضْرِبُ عَنْكم الذِّكْرَ صَفْحاً إنْ كُنْتُم﴾ (shall We then turn the Reminder away from you, disregarding you, if you are [a transgressing people]) and ﴿أَنْ كُنْتُمْ﴾ (because you are).
Similar is the poet's saying:
أتجزع أن بان الخلِيطُ المودّع * وحبل الصَّفَا من عَزَّة المتقطع
(Do you grieve because the departing companions have left, and because the rope of pure affection with ʿAzza is cut?)

farraa:8-8.t: His saying: ﴿صَعِيداً﴾ (ground): الصعيد is earth (dust). الجُرُز is that the land has no vegetation in it. One says: جُرِزَت الأرضُ (the land was laid bare), and it is مجرُوزة; and the locusts, or the sheep, or the camels جرَزها (laid it bare), i.e. ate what was on it.

farraa:9-9.t: His saying: ﴿أَمْ حَسِبْتَ﴾ (or did you think) addresses Muhammad ﷺ. ﴿أَنَّ أَصْحَابَ ٱلْكَهْفِ﴾ (that the companions of the cave): the cave is the mountain in which they took refuge. الرقيم (al-Raqīm) is a lead tablet on which their lineages, their religion, and what they fled from were written.

farraa:31-31.t:
His saying: ﴿يُحَلَّوْنَ فِيهَا مِنْ أَسَاوِرَ مِن ذَهَبٍ﴾ (they will be adorned therein with bracelets of gold): if you dropped (منْ) from "bracelets", it would be accusative. If you dropped (منْ) from "gold", its accusative would be permitted with some ugliness, because the number of the bracelets is not known; the accusative in the specifier (tamyīz (specification)) is good only when the number is known, as in your saying: عندى جُبَّتان خَزّا (I have two cloaks of silk-wool), وأسواران ذهباً (two bracelets of gold), and ثلاثة أساور ذهبا (three bracelets of gold). If you say: عندى أساور ذهباً without stating their number, it should be with من, because what is specified ought to be of known quantity. Similar is the saying of Allah, Blessed and Exalted: ﴿وَيُنَزِّلُ مِنَ السماءِ مِنْ جِبَالٍ فِيها مِنْ بَرَد﴾ (and He sends down from the sky, from mountains therein, of hail); the meaning is: in it are mountains of hail, and (من) came in because the mountains are not numbered in the wording. But it is permitted, as though by the mountains and the bracelets you meant "many"; as when someone says: "he has only two rings of gold" and you say: "he has rings of gold (خواتِم ذهباً)", since it is a rejoinder to something of known number. So treat the bracelets and "mountains of hail" in this manner.
As for (يُحَلّون), if someone said يَحْلَون it would be permitted, because the Arabs say: امرأة حالية (an adorned woman), and she حلِيت, so she تحلَى (is adorned), when she wears jewellery; she تحلَى حُلِيّاً and حلْياً.
His saying ﴿نِعْمَ ٱلثَّوَابُ﴾ (excellent is the reward): He did not say نعمت الثواب; and He said ﴿وَحَسُنَتْ مُرْتَفَقاً﴾ (and good is it as a resting place), making the verb feminine according to the sense of "Paradise"; had He made it masculine according to the masculine "resting place" it would have been correct, as He said ﴿وبِئْسَ المِهَادُ﴾ (and wretched is the resting place), ﴿وَبِئْسَ القَرَارُ﴾ (and wretched is the settlement), ﴿وبئس المَصِيرُ﴾ (and wretched is the destination), and as He said ﴿بئْسَ لِلظالِمينَ بَدَلاً﴾ (wretched it is for the wrongdoers as an exchange), meaning Iblīs and his offspring, and He did not say بئسوا.
(بئس) may also be for Iblīs alone. The Arabs keep نعم and بئس singular even when they come after the nouns, so they say: أَمّا قومُك فنِعْمُوا قوماً and نعم قوماً (as for your people, what an excellent people they are), and likewise بئس. Keeping them singular is permitted only because they are not verbs whose (verbal) meaning is sought; they were only brought in to indicate praise and blame. Do you not see that their form is that of فَعَل, but their meaning is not so, and that one does not say from them: يبأس الرجل زيد or ينعم الرجل أخوك. That is why they allowed both plural and singular in the verb. Their counterpart is ﴿عَسَى أَنْ يَكُونُوا خَيْراً مِنْهُمْ﴾ (perhaps they may be better than them); and in the reading of ʿAbdallāh: (عَسَوْا أَنْ يَكُونوا خـَيْراً مِنْهُمْ). Do you not see that you do not say هو يَعْسِى, just as you do not say يَبْأَس.

farraa:33-33.t:
His saying: ﴿كِلْتَا ٱلْجَنَّتَيْنِ آتَتْ أُكُلَهَا﴾ (each of the two gardens produced its fruit): He did not say آتتا (dual). That is because (كلتا) is two whose single one is not used alone; its origin is كُلّ, as you say of three: كلّ. So the rule was that the two should have what the plural has, not that something singular be used for one of them; so its singular (verb) was permitted [104b] «[Translator's note: "104 ب" is a manuscript folio marker.]» on the pattern of كلّ. And its being feminine is permitted because of the feminine marker that appears in كِلْتا. Do likewise with كلتا, كِلاَ and كُلّ when you put them in construct with a definite noun and the verb comes after them: use the plural or the singular. Of the singular is His saying ﴿وكُلُّهُمْ آتِيهِ يَوْمَ القِيَامَةِ فَرْداً﴾ (and all of them will come to Him on the Day of Resurrection alone), and of the plural ﴿وكُلٌّ أَتَوهُ دَاخِرِين﴾ (and all will come to Him humbled), and (آتوه) likewise. This is frequent in the Qurʾān and in other speech. The poet said:
وكلتاهما قد خُطّ لى فى صَحيفتى * فلا العَيْشُ أهواه ولا الموت أرْوح
(Both of them have been written for me in my record: I do not love life, nor is death more restful.)
The Arabs may use one of كلتا in the singular, meaning by the singular its two. One of them recited to me:
فى كِلت رجليهَا سُلاَمَى واحده * كلتاهما مقرونة بزائده
(In each of her two feet is a single toe-bone; both of them joined to an extra one.)
By كلت he means كلتا.
The Arabs also do this with (أىّ): they make it feminine or masculine while the meaning is feminine. Of that is the saying of Allah, Blessed and Exalted: ﴿وَمَا تَدْرِى نَفْسٌ بِأَىِّ أَرْضٍ تَمُوتُ﴾ (and no soul knows in which land it will die); in ordinary speech بأيَّة أرض is permitted. Similar is ﴿فى أَىِّ صُورة﴾ (in whatever form); in ordinary speech في أيَّة صورة is permitted. The poet said:
بأىّ بلاء أمْ بأيَّة نعمة * يقدَّم قبلى مُسلم والمُهَلَّب
(By what trial, or by what favour, are Muslim and al-Muhallab put ahead of me?)
And أيّتهُما قال ذاك (which of the two [fem.] said [masc.] that) is permitted, though وقالت ذاكَ is better. You use the masculine although you have added the hāʾ, imagining the hāʾ to be absent, since ﴿بأىّ أرضٍ تَمُوتُ﴾ is permitted for the feminine. Likewise you may say of two feminines: كلاهما and كلتاهما. The poet said:
كلا عقِبيه قد تشعّبَ رَأسُهَا * من الضرب فى جَنْبَىْ ثَفَالٍ مباشر
(Both his heels — their tips have split from striking the flanks of a sluggish camel, kicking it directly.)
الثفال: the slow camel.
If someone says: "You permitted the singular with (كلتا) only because one of its two is not used alone; so do you permit الاثنتان قام, using the singular, and الاثنان قام, since no singular of it is used alone?", I say: الاثنان (two) is built on a singular, whereas (كِلاَ) is not built on a singular. Do you not see that your saying قام عبدُالله كلُّه (ʿAbdallāh stood, all of him) is wrong; and that you find the meaning of "two" built on a singular, like the meaning of three and higher numbers; and only الاثنان قاما and الاثنتان قامَتَا (in the dual) is permitted.
It is in the reading of ʿAbdallāh:
* كُلّ الجنتين آتى أُكُله *
and its meaning is: everything of the fruit of the two gardens produced its fruit. Had he meant the sum of the two, and not all the fruit, only كلتاهما would be permitted; do you not see that you do not say: قامت المرأتان كلهما (the two women stood, all of them), because (كل) is not suitable for one of two women, whereas it is suitable for one of two gardens. So judge by these two cases everything that is divisible into parts, whether it can be portioned or not.
His saying ﴿وَفَجَّرْنَا خِلالَهُمَا نَهَراً﴾ (and We caused a river to gush forth within them): it may be asked: how is the doubled form permitted when the river is only one? I say: because the river extends, so that the gushing became as though it were throughout the whole of it; so the light and the heavy forms are both permitted in it. Similar is ﴿حتَّى تَفْجُرَ لَنَا مِنَ الأَرْضِ يَنْبُوعاً﴾ (until you cause a spring to gush forth for us from the earth), read with the heavy and the light form.

farraa:34-34.t: His saying: ﴿وَكَانَ لَهُ ثَمَرٌ﴾ (and he had fruit): Muḥammad told us: al-Farrāʾ told us: al-Muʿallā ibn Hilāl al-Juʿfī told me, from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid, who said: whatever in the Qurʾān is ثُمُر with ḍamma means wealth, and whatever is ثَمَر with fatḥa is from fruits.

farraa:36-36.t: His saying: ﴿خَيْراً مِّنْهَا مُنْقَلَباً﴾ (better than this as a return) refers back to the garden. In some of the codices of the people of Medina it is (منْهُما مُنْقَلَباً) (than the two), referring back to the two gardens.

farraa:38-38.t:
His saying: ﴿لَّٰكِنَّاْ هُوَ ٱللَّهُ رَبِّي﴾ (but as for me, He is Allah, my Lord): its meaning is: لكن أنا هو الله ربّى (but I — He is Allah, my Lord). The hamza of the alif of أنا was dropped, and the expression was used frequently, so the nūn of (أنا) was assimilated into the nūn of (لكن). Some Arabs say: أنا قلت ذاك (I said that) with the full alif, so it was read لكنّا according to that dialect; and the alif was kept in the codex for both dialects, just as they said رأيت يزيدا (I saw Yazīd) and قواريرا (flasks), the alif being kept in both in both usages when you pause. In other than the Qurʾān it is permitted to pause on أنا without alif. Some Arabs say, when pausing: أَنَهْ, and this is in a good dialect; it is in upper Tamīm and lower Qays. Abū Tharwān recited to me:
وترميننى بالطّرْف أىْ أنت مذنب * وتقلِيننى لكنّ إيّاكَ لا أَقلى
(You cast glances at me, meaning "you are at fault", and you hate me — but I, I do not hate you.)
He means: لكِنْ أنا إيّاك لا أَقلى; he dropped the hamza, so it became like a single word. Al-Kisāʾī claimed that he heard the Arabs say لكنَّ والله, meaning لكن أنا والله (but I, by Allah). And al-Kisāʾī said: I heard some Arabs say إنَّ قائم, meaning إنْ أنا قائم (I am not standing); he dropped the hamza and assimilated, so it is a counterpart of لكن.

farraa:39-39.t:
His saying: ﴿مَا شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ﴾ (what Allah wills): ما is in the position of the nominative. If you wish, you make it nominative by suppressing (هو), meaning: هو ما شاء الله (it is what Allah willed). And if you wish, you suppress ما شاء الله كان (what Allah willed came to be), dropping (كان); and then the position of (ما) is accusative by شاء, because the verb falls on it. Dropping the answer (jawāb) is permitted, as He said ﴿فإنِ اسْتَطَعْتَ أَنْ تَبْتَغىَ نَفَقَا فىِ الأرْضِ أَوْ سُلَّماً فىِ السَّماءِ﴾ (and if you are able to seek a tunnel into the earth or a ladder into the sky…), which has no answer because its meaning is known.
His saying: ﴿إِن تَرَنِ أَنَاْ أَقَلَّ مِنكَ﴾ (if you see me less than you): (أنا), when you make (أقلَّ) accusative, is an ʿimād (support pronoun); and when you make (أقل) nominative it is a noun (i.e. mubtadaʾ (subject)). Reading with both is permitted.

farraa:40-40.t: His saying: ﴿صَعِيداً زَلَقاً﴾ (slippery ground): الزلَق is earth with no vegetation on it, burnt and decayed.

farraa:41-41.t: [His saying:] ﴿مَآؤُهَا غَوْراً﴾ (its water sunken): the Arabs say: ماء غَوْر (sunken water), ماءان غَوْر (two sunken waters), and مِياه غوْر (sunken waters), with the singular in every case.

farraa:42-43.t:
His saying: ﴿خَاوِيَةٌ عَلَىٰ عُرُوشِهَا﴾ (fallen down upon its trellises): upon its roofs.
His saying: ﴿وَلَمْ تَكُن لَّهُ فِئَةٌ يَنصُرُونَهُ﴾ (and he had no party to help him): He referred (the plural verb) to the men. Had it been said تَنْصره, referring to the party (feminine) — as He said ﴿(فِئَةٌ) تُقَاتِلُ فىِ سَبيلِ اللهِ وَأُخْرَى كَافِرَةٌ﴾ (one party fighting in the way of Allah and another disbelieving) — it would have been permitted.

farraa:44-44.t: His saying: ﴿هُنَالِكَ ٱلْوَلاَيَةُ لِلَّهِ ٱلْحَقُّ﴾ (there, the authority is Allah's, the True): (الحقّ) is nominative as a naʿt (adjective) of (الولاية). In the reading of Ubayy: (هُنَالِكَ ٱلْوَلاَيَةُ ٱلْحَقُّ لِلَّه) (there, the true authority is Allah's). If you wish you make it genitive, making it a naʿt of (الله). الوِلاية is sovereignty. Had you made (الحقّ) accusative in the sense of "truly" (حقّا), it would have been correct.

farraa:45-45.t:
His saying: ﴿تَذْرُوهُ ٱلرِّياحُ﴾ (the winds scatter it): from ذَرَوت, and ذَرَيْت is a dialect form; it is thus in the reading of ʿAbdallāh: (تَذْرِيه الريح). Had a reader read (تُذْريه الريح), from أذريت, i.e. it throws it down, that would be a valid aspect. Al-Mufaḍḍal recited to me:
فقلت له صوِّب ولا تجهَدَنَّهُ * فيُذرِكَ منْ أُخْرى القطاةِ فتَزْلَقِ
(I said to him: go gently and do not tire it out, lest it throw you off the back of its croup and you slip.)
You say: أذريت الرجل عن الدابَّة and عن البعير, i.e. I threw him off the riding animal or the camel.

farraa:46-46.t:
His saying: ﴿وَٱلْبَاقِيَاتُ ٱلصَّالِحَاتُ﴾ (and the enduring good deeds): it is said they are the five prayers, and it is said they are: Subḥān Allāh, al-ḥamdu li-llāh, lā ilāha illā Allāh and Allāhu akbar.
His saying: ﴿وَخَيْرٌ أَمَلاً﴾ (and better for hope): (he says: the best of what is hoped for); and hope for a good deed is better than hope for an evil deed.

farraa:47-47.t:
His saying ﴿وَيَوْمَ نُسَيِّرُ ٱلْجِبَالَ﴾ (and the day We will set the mountains moving), and His saying: ﴿وَتَرَى ٱلأَرْضَ بَارِزَةً﴾ (and you will see the earth laid bare): he says: We brought its people out from its belly. It is also said: the mountains were moved away from it, so it all became exposed, no part of it concealing another.
His saying: ﴿فَلَمْ نُغَادِرْ مِنْهُمْ﴾ (and We will not leave behind any of them): this is the reading (and had it been read "ولم نغْدِرْ" it would have been correct); their meaning is one. One says: ما أغدرت منهم أحداً and ما غادرت (I left none of them behind). One of them recited to me:
هل لك والعائض منهم عائِض * فى هجمة يغدرمنها القابض * سُدْسا ورُبعا تحتها فرائض *
(Would you like — and the one who gives in exchange is giving in exchange — a herd of camels from which the receiver leaves behind sudus and rubʿ camels, with obligatory-alms camels beneath them?)
Al-Farrāʾ said: sudus and rubʿ are among the ages of camels.

farraa:50-50.t: His saying: ﴿فَفَسَقَ عَنْ أَمْرِ رَبِّهِ﴾ (and he departed from the command of his Lord): i.e. he went out from obedience to his Lord. The Arabs say: فَسَقت الرُّطَبة (the fresh date came out) of its (skin) and its peel, because it comes out of it. It seems the mouse was called فُوَيْسِقة only because it comes out of its hole upon people.

farraa:52-52.t: His saying: ﴿وَجَعَلْنَا بَيْنَهُم مَّوْبِقاً﴾ (and We will put between them a place of ruin): it is said: We made their ties in this world (مَوْبَقاً), he says: a cause of destruction for them in the Hereafter. It is also said that it is a valley in Hell.

farraa:53-53.t: His saying: ﴿فَظَنُّوۤاْ أَنَّهُمْ مُّوَاقِعُوهَا﴾ (and they will think that they are to fall into it): i.e. they will know.

farraa:55-55.t: His saying: ﴿وَمَا مَنَعَ ٱلنَّاسَ أَن يُؤْمِنُوۤاْ﴾ (and nothing has prevented the people from believing): it is said that "the people" here is in the sense of a single man. His saying ﴿إِلاَّ أَن تَأْتِيَهُمْ سُنَّةُ ٱلأَوَّلِينَ﴾ (except that the way of the former peoples should come to them): أن is in the position of the nominative. His saying ﴿سُنَّةُ ٱلأَوَّلِينَ﴾: he says: Our way in destroying the nations that denied. His saying ﴿أَوْ يَأْتِيَهُمُ ٱلْعَذَابُ قُبُلاً﴾ (or the punishment should come to them before their eyes): openly. (قِبَلاً) may have this meaning; and (قُبُلاً) may be as though it were a plural of قَبِيل — and قُبُل — i.e. punishment of different kinds, one following another.

farraa:58-58.t:
His saying: ﴿لَّن يَجِدُواْ مِن دُونِهِ مَوْئِلاٍ﴾ (they will never find besides it an escape): (الموئل is the place of escape), and it is the place of refuge; in meaning they are one. The Arabs say: إنه ليوائل إلى موضعه, meaning: he goes to his place and his stronghold.
The poet said:
لا وألت نفسك خلَّيتها * للعامريّين ولم تُكْلَم
(May your soul find no escape! You abandoned it to the ʿĀmirīs and you were not even wounded.)
(He means: may it not be saved.)

farraa:59-59.t:
His saying: ﴿لِمَهْلِكِهِم مَّوْعِداً﴾ (for their destruction an appointed time): he says: for Our destroying them, (موعداً) a fixed term. ʿĀṣim read (لمَهْلَكهِمْ), with fatḥa on the mīm and the lām; and (لمهِلِكهم) «[Translator's note: so the text; i.e. لِمَهْلِكِهِم.]» with kasra on the lām is permitted, building it on هَلَك يَهْلِك. Whoever wants the noun (of place/time) from a verb whose imperfect has kasra on the ʿayn gives mafʿil kasra; whoever wants the maṣdar (verbal noun) gives the ʿayn fatḥa — like المضرِب and المضرَب, المَدِبّ and المَدَبّ, المفِرّ and المَفَرّ. When the yafʿal (imperfect) has fatḥa on the ʿayn, the Arabs prefer fatḥa on it in mafʿal, whether noun or maṣdar. Sometimes they give the ʿayn kasra in mafʿil when they mean the noun by it; some of them said ﴿مَجْمِعَ البَحْرَيْنِ﴾ (the meeting place of the two seas), and that is the analogical form, though it is rare.
When the yafʿul has ḍamma on the ʿayn, like يدخل and يخرج, the Arabs prefer fatḥa on the ʿayn in both the noun and the maṣdar from it — except certain nouns to which they have made kasra on the ʿayn in mafʿil obligatory. Among them: المسجِد (mosque), المطلِع (place of rising), المغرِب (west), المشرِق (east), المسقِط (place of falling), المفرِق (parting of the hair), المجزِر (slaughter place), المسكِن (dwelling), المَرْفِق from رَفَق يَرْفُق, المنسِك from نَسَك يَنْسُك, and المنبت.
So they made kasra the mark of the noun and fatḥa the mark of the maṣdar. Sometimes some Arabs give it fatḥa (in the noun); مسكِن and مسكَن have both been read. We have heard المسجِد and المسجَد when they meant the noun, and المطلَع and المطلِع. Fatḥa (naṣb) is permitted in all of it; even if you have not heard it, do not reject it if it comes.
Whatever is from (roots with final) yāʾ and wāw, like دعوت and قضيت, its mafʿal has fatḥa, whether noun or maṣdar — except المأقِى (the inner corner) of the eye, for the Arabs gave this word kasra. Some Arabs call the shelter of camels مَأْوِى. These two are rare. They refrained from (giving kasra to the ʿayn) with yāʾ and wāw only because the yāʾ and the wāw disappear in pause on account of the nunation that attaches, so they turned it into alif, since that does not drop in pause.
When the mafʿal is from كال يكيل (to measure) and similar verbs, the noun from it has kasra and the maṣdar fatḥa; of that is مال مَمِيلا and مَمَالا: you take the kasra to the nouns and the fatḥa to the maṣdars. Had you given both fatḥa, or both kasra, in the maṣdar and the noun, it would be permitted. The Arabs say المعاش (livelihood), and they have said المعيش. Ruʾba ibn al-ʿAjjāj said:
إليك اشكو شدّة المعيش * ومرّ أعوام نتَفْن ريشى * نتف الحُبَارَى عن قَرَا رَهِيشِ *
(To You I complain of the hardness of living [106a] «[Translator's note: "106 ا" is a manuscript folio marker.]», and of the passing of years that have plucked my feathers, as the bustard is plucked from a lean back.)
القَرَا: the back. And another said:
أنا الرجل الذى قد عبتموهُ * ومَا فيكم لَعَيّاب مَعَاب
(I am the man whom you have found fault with, yet there is nothing in you for a fault-finder to fault.)
Similar are مَسَار and مَسِير; and whatever resembles it is like it.
When the yafʿal from (roots with middle) yāʾ and wāw has fatḥa, like يخاف and يهاب, the noun and the maṣdar from it both have fatḥa, like المخاف and المهاب.
Whatever is from wāw with ḍamma, like يقوم, يقول, يعود, يقود and the like, the noun and the maṣdar in it both have fatḥa. They gave it fatḥa even when intending the noun, and did not give it kasra as المَغْرِب was given kasra, only because they disliked the wāw turning into yāʾ, so that the wāw would be confused with the yāʾ.
Whatever begins with wāw, like وزنت, ورثت and وجِلت, its mafʿil, whether noun or maṣdar, has kasra; as in His saying ﴿أَنْ لَنْ نَجْعَلَ لَكُمْ مَوْعِداً﴾ (that We would never make for you an appointment). Likewise يَوْحَل and يَوْحَل «[Translator's note: so the text, the word repeated; perhaps يَوْجَل and يَوْحَل.]»: the mafʿil from both has kasra (in both aspects). Al-Kisāʾī claimed that he heard مَوْجَل and مَوْحَل. Al-Farrāʾ said: and I heard «[Translator's note: the text has "ويمعت", evidently وسمعت.]» موضَع. They gave kasra to what begins with wāw only because when the verb in it has fatḥa it is of two kinds: as for the transitive, its wāw drops, like وَزَن يزِنُ; and the intransitive keeps its wāw in yafʿal. The maṣdars are the same for the transitive and the intransitive, so they made no distinction in their two maṣdars; distinctions are only in faʿala/yafʿilu.
Whatever has hamza is with fatḥa in both cases. It is as though they built it on yafʿal, because what has hamza as its lām (third radical) comes with fatḥa on the ʿayn, from faʿala and from faʿila. If you say: "What if they gave it kasra intending the noun, as they gave kasra to مجمِع?", I say: it has not come. It is as though they treated the hamzated (root) like the yāʾ and the wāw, because the hamza may be dropped, so it joins them.
Whatever mafʿal is derived from afʿaltu (the fourth form), you may give the mīm of its noun and its maṣdar ḍamma; and you may produce it according to its original form before the alif was added to it. So you say: أخرجته مُخْرجاً and مَخْرجاً (I brought him out), and أنزلته مُنْزَلاً and مَنْزِلاً (I lodged him). It has been read: ﴿أَنْزِلْنِى مُنْزَلاَ مُبَارَكاً﴾ (land me at a blessed landing place), ﴿وَأَنْتَ خَيْرُ المُنْزِلِينِ﴾ (and You are the best to accommodate [us]), and ﴿مَنْزِلا﴾.
Whatever is an instrument with which work is done, like المِرْوحة (fan), المِطرقة (hammer) and the like, with or without the hāʾ (tāʾ marbūṭa), has kasra on the mīm and fatḥa on the ʿayn; like المِدْرع, المِلحف, المِطرق and the like. However, they said: المَطهرة and المِطهرة (vessel for purification), المَرقاة and المِرقاة (ladder), المَسقاة and المِسقاة (watering vessel). Whoever gives it kasra likens it to the instrument with which work is done; whoever gives it fatḥa says: this is a place in which something is done, so he made it different and gave the mīm fatḥa.
